broker_url.description: URL of the message broker (e.g., Redis or RabbitMQ). Must be reachable by workers and producers.

result_backend.description: Backend where task results are stored. Often a separate Redis DB or database.

task_serializer.description: Serialization method for outgoing task messages (e.g., 'json', 'pickle'). JSON is safer and interoperable. For security, 'json' is recommended to prevent arbitrary code execution from untrusted brokers.

result_serializer.description: Serialization method for task results (e.g., 'json', 'pickle'). For security, 'json' is recommended.

accept_content.description: List of allowed content types for incoming task messages. Prevents unsafe deserialization. Should only include serializers you trust and use.

task_time_limit.description: Hard time limit for a task (seconds). Exceeding this kills the worker executing it.

task_soft_time_limit.description: Soft time limit (seconds). Triggers a warning exception but allows graceful cleanup.

worker_max_tasks_per_child.description: Maximum tasks a worker process handles before being replaced (helps prevent memory leaks).

worker_concurrency.description: Number of concurrent worker processes. 0 = auto-detect CPU count. Adjust for I/O-bound vs CPU-bound tasks.

worker_prefetch_multiplier.description: Tasks prefetched per worker. Lower values improve fairness; 0 = unlimited.

task_default_queue.description: Default queue name for tasks without explicit routing.

task_routes.description: List of task routing rules. Each rule maps tasks to specific queues/exchanges.

task_result_expires.description: Time (seconds) after which task results are deleted from the backend.

timezone.description: Timezone for scheduled tasks and logs (e.g., 'UTC', 'Europe/London').

worker_send_events.description: Enable event streaming (e.g., for Flower or real-time monitoring).

worker_log_level.description: Minimum log level for worker logs (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL).

beat_schedule.description: List of periodic (beat) tasks. Each item defines schedule and arguments.

task_eager_propagates.description: If true, task exceptions are raised immediately (e.g., for sync tasks).

task_acks_late.description: If true, tasks are acknowledged only after successful completion (prevents message loss).

task_reject_on_worker_lost.description: If true, tasks are requeued when a worker dies before acknowledgment.
